title: Anchorpoint file locking docs: auto-lock binaries, release on push

pins.note: Locked files are write-protected; a user thumbnail shows who holds the lock
Binaries auto-lock on modify, unlock on push; text files opt-in
With the Unreal plugin, editor checkout replaces auto-locking
Separate section: Git LFS locks are a different system, not used

insight: Anchorpoint makes locking invisible: modifying a binary locks it, pushing releases it, and an avatar shows the owner. It does this with its own metadata server, not Git LFS locks.
gitgud: Claude's pick: copy the auto-lock-on-modify and release-on-push mechanics, but on standard LFS locks so it works with any host and no extra server.

title: Anchorpoint main window: timeline, changed files with thumbnails, 3D preview

pins.note: Timeline of commits per person replaces a branch graph
Single message box + Sync button: commit and push in one step
Changed files grouped by folder, each with a thumbnail
FBX opened in an inline 3D viewer with version picker

insight: The artist-facing flow is one list of changed files with thumbnails and a single Sync action; the 3D preview sits next to the list.
gitgud: Claude's pick: give binary rows real thumbnails and an inline preview pane, but keep stage/commit/push explicit for a programmer like Max.

title: Anchorpoint Unity guide: lock scenes/prefabs, plugin required

pins.note: .unity and .prefab files are lockable, binaries should always be locked
Auto-configures LFS and a Unity .gitignore template
Unity plugin is the only way locking works properly
Smart Merge still set up by hand in .git/config

insight: Even a dedicated game Git client leaves UnityYAMLMerge as a manual config step and needs a Unity plugin because Unity ignores read-only files.
gitgud: Claude's pick: auto-detect UnityYAMLMerge from Unity Hub installs and wire it per repo with one click.

title: Anchorpoint pricing: locking and selective checkout are paid Team features

pins.note: Free plan: GitHub only, non-commercial
Team: EUR 20/user/month billed yearly
File locking only in the paid tier
Selective (sparse) checkout also paid
Self-hosted lock/metadata server only in Organization

insight: The game-dev features (locks, partial checkout) are the paywall; the Git client itself is free for personal use.
gitgud: Claude's pick: ship locks and sparse checkout free in gitgud, since they're thin wrappers over git-lfs and git.

title: UVCS Smart Locks: lock rules, latest-revision check, retained locks

pins.note: Checkout vs Lock and checkout; rules turn checkout into a lock
Only the latest revision can be locked, so no stale edits
One org-wide lock rule plus per-repo rules
Check-in on a side branch = Retained until merged to main

insight: Smart Locks tie locks to a destination branch: you can only lock the newest version, and the lock follows your change until it is merged.
gitgud: Claude's pick: warn before locking if your local copy of the file is behind origin/main (cheap with gix), mirroring the latest-revision rule.

title: Gluon: pick files to load into a partial workspace

pins.note: Configure: tick files and folders to download
Search by pattern (*.jpg, *.psd) to select
MaxPreviewFileSize key in client.conf
Unloaded files preview only up to 1 MiB

insight: Artists work in a partial workspace chosen file by file, with previews of files they have not downloaded.
gitgud: Claude's pick: a folder-tree 'load / unload' view that drives git sparse-checkout plus lfs.fetchinclude, with previews fetched lazily.

title: P4V file badges: yours red, other users blue, lock, out of date

pins.note: Red badges = your actions
Blue badges = another user's actions
Lock icon: global lock blocks others
Blue check: someone else has it checked out
Yellow triangle: your copy is not the latest

insight: Perforce answers 'who has this file and is my copy stale' with a two-colour badge system on every file, plus hover tooltips.
gitgud: Claude's pick: per-file badges for 'locked by me', 'locked by X', and 'newer on remote' in the file tree, with the owner in a tooltip.

title: Diversion Connect for Unity: in-editor commit panel and conflict alerts

pins.note: Docked panel lists changed assets and metas with status tags
Commit message and commit straight from the editor
Alerts when you open/save a file a teammate is editing
Colour status overlays in the Project window

insight: Diversion warns about concurrent edits at open/save time inside Unity rather than blocking them, which Unity's ignore-read-only behaviour makes necessary.
gitgud: Claude's pick: keep the main app outside Unity; a small optional Unity package that only shows lock state and asks before editing a locked file is enough (open: v1 or later).

title: Git LFS file locking: lockable attribute, lock/locks/unlock

pins.note: git lfs track --lockable marks a pattern lockable
.gitattributes gets the lockable attribute
Lockable files become read-only until you lock them
git lfs locks lists path, owner, lock ID
Push continues if the server lacks the locking API

insight: The whole locking model is already in git-lfs (attribute, read-only enforcement, lock IDs, push verification); it just has no good GUI.
gitgud: Claude's pick: build the lock panel on git lfs locks --verify --json and git lfs lock/unlock --json, no custom server.

title: Unity 6.3 Smart merge: what UnityYAMLMerge merges and how it's wired

pins.note: Merges .unity, .prefab and .meta semantically
.asset/.mat/.controller need --force, else fallback tool
With exclusive locks on scenes/prefabs you don't need Smart Merge
Premerge/Ask modes exist only for Perforce in the editor

insight: Unity documents UnityYAMLMerge only as an interactive mergetool for Git; scope is scenes, prefabs and metas, and other YAML assets are excluded by default.
gitgud: Claude's pick: register it as a git merge driver for .unity/.prefab/.meta (spike to verify exit codes) and always show a structural review of 'clean' merges.

title: Unity 6.3 editor VCS operations: Perforce vs UVCS, none for Git

pins.note: Only Perforce and UVCS columns: Git has no editor integration
UVCS cannot Get Latest from the Project view
Perforce can check out asset and .meta together or separately
UVCS conflicts must be resolved in its own GUI
Lock/Unlock: Perforce yes, UVCS no

insight: Unity's built-in VCS hooks give Perforce users checkout, lock and resolve in the editor; Git users get only visible .meta files.
gitgud: Claude's pick: treat asset+meta as one unit in gitgud's own UI, since Unity won't help Git users do it.

title: Unreal Git plugin: fast LFS locking and Status Branches

pins.note: Multi-threaded lock/unlock for many files at once
Status Branches: flag files changed on other remote branches
No prebuilt binaries; compile it yourself
Needs explicit *.uasset / *.umap .gitattributes lines

insight: Production Unreal teams on Git needed lock batching, a local lock cache and cross-branch 'outdated' detection to make LFS locks usable.
gitgud: Claude's pick: batch lock/unlock calls, cache lock state locally, and flag files modified on configured remote branches (a Status Branches equivalent).

title: GitHub Git LFS billing: metered storage and bandwidth

pins.note: $0 budget: LFS blocked for the rest of the month
Every download bills the repo owner's bandwidth
1-byte change to a 500 MB file = another 500 MB stored
GitHub Actions LFS downloads count too

insight: LFS cost is driven by whole-file re-uploads and every clone/CI download, which is why game teams get surprise budget lockouts.
gitgud: Claude's pick: show the LFS bytes a push will add before pushing, and a local cache/prune panel.

title: GitLab file locking: LFS exclusive locks vs default-branch locks

pins.note: Exclusive LFS locks on all tiers, block every branch
UI default-branch locks are Premium/Ultimate only
Other branches stay editable but show Lock status
Fork sync bypasses default-branch locks

insight: GitLab exposes standard LFS locks everywhere and adds a host-side lock that blocks merge requests into the default branch.
gitgud: Claude's pick: rely on standard LFS locks (portable across GitHub, GitLab, Azure, Gitea) and only link out to host-specific lock pages.

title: Version control and asset sharing tools by studio size, 2025

pins.note: Perforce: 45% AAA, 10% mid/indie, 3% hobbyist
GitHub: 61% mid/indie, 79% hobbyist
Unity Version Control: 0% AAA, 9% mid/indie
Google Drive still used for art by a third of teams

insight: Below AAA, game dev runs on GitHub and Git; Perforce is an AAA tool and UVCS is niche. Art still travels outside version control a lot.
gitgud: Claude's pick: target Git + LFS on GitHub-class hosts for Unity indies and mid-size teams, Max's own segment.

title: Fork issue: artists want unlock-on-push for LFS locks

pins.note: Request: 'unlock pushed files' checkbox after push
Fork dev: technically impossible, push is per branch
Manual unlocking after every push is too much for artists
Fork has only a manual Repository > Git LFS > Locks list

insight: A mainstream Git GUI has lock/unlock but leaves the post-push unlock to the user, and artists drop it; the dev considers automatic unlock infeasible.
gitgud: Claude's pick: after a push, diff the pushed range against my locks and offer a pre-ticked unlock list; that is computable from the pushed commits.

title: Epic's Lore repo: open-source VCS for game-scale binaries

pins.note: 9.2k stars within months of the June 2026 release
v0.14.0: pre-1.0, formats may still change
lore-fuse: virtual filesystem for lazy file loading
Written in Rust, like gitgud-core
Repo ships .claude/skills: agent-assisted development

insight: Epic's Lore is a centralized, chunked, Rust VCS aimed at Perforce users; locking is advisory today and Unity/Git interop is not on its roadmap.
gitgud: Claude's pick: watch it, don't target it in v1; keep gitgud-core's VCS calls behind one module so a Lore backend stays possible (open).
